characters.name: Porter Idris Bello
characters.role: Carries goods along the south road

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: News? Oh, have you heard? Every blade from Hesper's forge shatters in the cold, and the guild is hiding it! Idris the porter told me. Everyone is saying it.

options.text: Thanks. I'll keep my ears open.

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: Where? I didn't ask. He carries goods all day, he hears everything. Ask him yourself, by the south road.

dialogue.speaker: porter-idris
dialogue.text: The blades? Yes. I heard that several of Hesper's blades cracked last winter, and the guild kept quiet about it. I may have said it a bit louder at the tea stall. Hana at the cloth stall told me first.

dialogue.speaker: porter-idris
dialogue.text: Heavy load today. If you find out where that blade story began, I'd like to know too.

dialogue.speaker: stallkeeper-hana
dialogue.text: One test piece. That’s what my sister copied out for me. I never saw it crack. On market day there were four chalk marks beside my stall. Four people had heard something. Want to look?

options.text: Find the dated guild entry she copied.
Follow the four chalk marks to the fruit stall.

dialogue.speaker: stallkeeper-hana
dialogue.text: Fine cloth from the river farms. And no more blade stories from me, I promise.

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: The kettle has boiled three times since Hesper left. The tea seller rubs a clean patch on the handle. “What am I going to tell the next person who asks?”

options.text: One test blade cracked last winter. Bring over the open record.
It was all lies. Hesper's blades never cracked.
Corvan started it to sell his own blades.
Carry the record straight to the night shift.
Unfold the four chalk marks beside the dated entry.

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: “Nothing happened?” She takes one cup down from the shelf. “I’d like Hana to be able to buy tea here tomorrow.”

options.text: Let me say it again, more carefully.
Let Hana read the dated entry beside the kettle.

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: The seller sets out another cup. “His brother comes through after dark. Can you give him anything sturdier than a guess about his family?”

options.text: You are right. Let me say what the record shows.
Take both versions to the night shift in person.

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: “One failure, three later checks. If the next piece breaks, our notice must still be true.” She takes a tag from the kettle. “We could hang the date here or walk it down to the late shift.”

options.text: Tie a dated correction to the kettle.
Walk the correction to the night shift.
Fold the four echoes alongside the guild entry.

dialogue.speaker: lumen
dialogue.text: A moth taps the rim of a cup. Lumen cups a hand behind it. “It sounds like two from over here.”

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: “Hesper sat here this morning. Same chipped blue cup.” She lifts it by the handle. “We talked about her boots.”

dialogue.speaker: stallkeeper-hana
dialogue.text: “North edge of the market. The clerk chained the book to the stand. It’s public, even when the guild doors are shut.”

dialogue.speaker: stallkeeper-hana
dialogue.text: Hana folds the price corner of a linen scrap around your thumb. “Four strokes with four kinds of chalk. Ask the fruit seller what each buyer heard.”

dialogue.speaker: fruit-seller
dialogue.text: The pear seller uncurls the price sheet. Four hands marked it. A grocer names Idris. Two cousins heard the grocer. The carter learned it from a cousin. The bottom corner is dark with rain.

options.text: Unfold the wet corner with the seller.
Leave the sheet here and check the open guild book.

dialogue.speaker: fruit-seller
dialogue.text: Four voices on the chalk sheet, one porter at the start. “I made the fourth stroke,” the seller says. “I wanted my sister to see how many of us cared. Has anyone seen the original entry?”

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: She threads the date and the single recorded failure through the kettle handle. Hesper reads it in the queue. Someone behind her has time to ask for the book. The night crew misses this pot.

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: You carry the open page to the night cart. Idris reads it to his brother and starts again when the wheel squeaks over a word. Back at the stall the tea has gone cold.

dialogue.speaker: villager-1
dialogue.text: Hana folds the four chalk strokes under the one name they lead to. The clerk slips the fold beside the dated account. A reader can trace the voices. They have to open the book to hear them.

missions.title: Side quest: The Shattering Rumour
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What happens to a claim each time it is retold?

objectives.title: Optional: ask Idris the porter where he heard the blade story.
Optional: ask Hana at the cloth stall where she heard it.
Read the dated guild entry. Follow Hana’s chalk sheet at the fruit stall if you want another lead.
Help the tea seller choose where the correction will travel.

hints.text: The tea seller named who told her.
Idris carries goods along the south road.
Find the porter south of the market and talk to him.
Idris stands on the south road, below the market square.
Idris named who told him first.
Hana sells cloth in the market.
Find the cloth stall and ask Hana.
Hana stands at the west side of the market square, near the fountain.
Hana says she read it somewhere anyone can read.
The guild keeps a public record book.
The record book stands at the north edge of the market, west of the guild hall.
Read the guild's record book on its stand near the bench, north-west of the fountain.
Compare each version with the record. What was added each time?
Say only what the record shows: no more, and no less.
'All lies' says less than the record. 'Corvan did it' adds a new claim with no source.
Take the dated page to the tea stall. You can leave a tag there, visit the late shift, or bring the fruit stall’s chalk account alongside.

journal.text: I traced a market story back to one recorded failure. Three checks came later. The date and the voices told me different things. Where we left the correction shaped who could hear it.
